analysis.title: What's Top of Mind in Macro Research: A blue tsunami, mixed central bank moves, US/Europe earnings growth
key_insights: Democrats won much larger-than-expected majorities across the House and Senate. GS expects them to use upcoming fiscal deadlines to seek concessions: limit the Iran war, roll back select tariffs, and reverse recently-enacted spending cuts.
The Brent oil risk premium has declined significantly after the midterm results. GS still sees downside risks to Middle East oil supply that could raise the premium again.
GS raised its average 2027 Brent forecast to $88/bbl from $80/bbl, and raised its 2027 TTF gas price forecasts.

The higher energy forecasts lead GS to expect weaker growth and higher inflation in Europe in 2027: growth of 0.9% vs 1.3% previously, peak core inflation 2.9% vs 2.7%, and peak headline inflation 4.1% vs 3.9%.

Democratic wins at state and local levels will have significant implications for AI and data center regulation. GS equity analysts think this could negatively affect select US utilities and Independent Power Producers (IPPs). GS expects the data center issue to fade somewhat and any moratoria on data center development to be short-lived.

GS expects the BoE to deliver its first rate hike of the cycle at the 5 November meeting and sees a second hike in February 2027 as more likely than not, given energy price pressure and strong UK activity and labor data.

GS thinks market pricing of about 100bp of BoE tightening by mid-2027 is too hawkish, leaving an already-expensive Sterling vulnerable. Recent fiscal developments should support Sterling near term, so GS lowered its EUR/GBP forecasts to 0.83/0.84/0.86 for 3/6/12 months (from 0.86/0.87/0.88).

The BoJ held rates as expected. GS pulled forward its next hike forecast to December from January 2027, citing Governor Ueda's hawkish comments and receding bond market concerns about Japan's fiscal health. Faster BoJ hikes, AI-related volatility and a potential GPIF allocation shift should support JPY near term.
EM central bank moves are mixed. Bank of Mexico may hold, following Brazil, though hold vs cut is a close call. The Czech National Bank will likely hike.
The PBOC shifted its policy rate benchmark from the 7-day reverse repo rate to the overnight reverse repo rate. GS views this as equivalent to a 5-10bp cut to front-end interbank rates.
US earnings growth has been strong but is likely peaking. GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth to slow from nearly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027.
European earnings have been more resilient than the domestic economy suggests, owing to sector composition and geographic exposure. GS raised its 2026/2027 STOXX 600 EPS growth forecasts to 18%/7%.
GS estimates October nonfarm payrolls rose 75k, modestly above consensus, with unemployment unchanged at 4.2% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% month-over-month.

The labor market impact of AI is broadening. GS sees early signs that workers displaced from AI-exposed jobs face harder transitions back into work and are moving into jobs at risk of further displacement.
